dateline: DAY 4342 — AUGUST 2026 — FORMER GUERRERO GOVERNOR ARRESTED, LINKED TO TRIAL
heroHeadline: Former Guerrero Governor Ángel Aguirre Arrested, Charged With Concealing Ayotzinapa Evidence
heroSubtitle: The FGR arrested former Guerrero Governor Ángel Aguirre Rivero on August 6, accusing him of ordering the destruction of security-camera footage showing police intercepting bus 1531 on the night of the disappearances. A judge formally linked him to trial for forced disappearance on August 12 — the highest-ranking civilian official charged in the case to date — after a 14-hour hearing; his defense announced it will appeal. Families and Tlachinollan called it 'a drop of hope' but warned accountability must extend to federal and military authorities. Separately, an appellate court ratified preventive prison for Army officer Pirita Ochoa on August 14, and families marched for the 142nd monthly Global Action on July 26, reaffirming they remain 'far from knowing the truth' nearly 12 years on.
footerNote: Data compiled from GIEI reports (I–VI), Mexican Truth Commission, CNDH Recommendation 208VG/2026, EAAF forensic reports, IACHR/OHCHR statements, and investigative journalism (Proceso, Infobae, La Jornada, Tlachinollan). All contested claims are marked.
